actions.label: Provide food rations to guards and their families
Provide an ongoing, regular food supply to the camp
Have guards organize and implement distribution through existing guard structures block by block
Permit FWB nutritional assessments under camp security arrangements
Distribute FWB food equally to all refugees without skimming, exclusion, or confiscation
Approve generator parts and secure fuel supply for the camp
Hire and prioritize local workers and suppliers, including MASHA
Share camp population registration data with FWB
Allow refugee input on the aid they receive
Run food distribution through existing guard and militia structures
Follow the camp's block-by-block distribution procedure
Accept coordinated, escorted FWB presence in the camp with no unrestricted movement

goals.label: Aid accountability and documentation meeting donor requirements
Camp authorities and guards control food distribution
Camp generators kept running with fuel and parts
Camp receives a steady ongoing food supply
Camp remains stable without riots, violence or perimeter breaches
Commander's authority and appearance of strength
FWB staff access and movement inside the camp
Food is distributed fairly to all refugees without discrimination
Guards and their families are fed and paid enough to stay loyal
Host town economy and goodwill, with local actors prioritized
Refugees are contained and do not reach the capital
Refugees have a say in the aid they receive
Refugees receive enough food and nutrition
Resource-heavy outsider procedures such as nutritional assessments
Safety of FWB staff and assistants from threats or violence
Commander's personal safety and legal exposure
Commander's standing with the Senior Militia Leader
Food aid diverted to guards, militia or resale
Food reaches people the militia labels terrorists or troublemakers
Reliable information on refugees' nutritional status
Working relationships with aid partners such as MASHA

redLines.label: Allow FWB and its chosen local assistants to manage food disbursement directly
redLines.quote: If FWB hires local independent laborers for the food distribution, you cannot trust those people not to stir unrest and even potentially support hidden terrorists by sharing items or information.

redLines.label: Have FWB staff and FWB-chosen local assistants carry out food disbursement
redLines.quote: If FWB hires local independent laborers for the food distribution, you cannot trust those people not to stir unrest and even potentially support hidden terrorists by sharing items or information.

assumptions: Commitments are binding and additive.
Goals and goal-action links were each extracted 3 times by a model; only those found in a majority of runs are kept.
Actions are chosen to bring about as much goal value as possible, within the solver's size limit.
Our values are the median of stances elicited from our role card.
The opponent column is the expected value of an elicited stance distribution (shared documents only); each opponent reading is one draw from it, independently per goal.
Stance labels map to numbers by a fixed scale (game.stance_values), not a measured utility.

Red lines and must-haves come from our role card, each with a verbatim quote. No plan may include a red-line action, leave out a must-have, or pass through a state worth less to us than our BATNA (the bottom line).
